World War 2 in Europe Unconditional Surrender! World War 2 in Europe is a strategic level game covering the World War Two’s European Theater. Players control the political decisions and military forces of the Axis, Western, and Soviet factions that struggled for European dominance and survival. With its emphasis on force projection and decision making, players focus on the big picture of managing military fronts and political opportunities. Through the use of simple mechanics and low on-map counter density, players easily handle the strategic action without a myriad of complicated subsystems or tall stacks of counters. Though the focus is on the big picture, the game delivers historical detail. Each country in the game has an historical army level order of battle, and the relative strength of its economy and national will to fight are effectively and simply modeled. Also represented are such World War II events as airdrops, Free Forces, jets, naval evacuation, partisans, radar, heavy artillery, and ULTRA; all of which are woven into the game's core mechanics for ease of play. Unconditional Surrender!has 16 scenarios ranging from individual campaigns to the entire war. Number of players: 1 - 3 Game duration: 12 mn Complexity: 5 / 5 Play Unconditional Surrender! [Rating: 1/10] The most ugly map ever conceived making Scandinavia the size of half of Europe. Using a different projection just to be different was a stupid idea, the counter artwork are horrible. It just looks like GMT had no control over whatever the designer submitted because the whole game feels like some school project and never got out of the "playtest stage". I watched a game being played on that cheap paper map and felt sad for everyone.  Next time stop trying to be different just to be different and recognize their is a reason why 99.9999999999% of all the other Europe maps use the CORRECT projecti

[Rating: 1/10] Total waste of money! Stupid map. Long and incomprehensibly rules. Too much counters for no any use. Not historical (in every AAR Yugoslavs are on the Eastern Front!!!). Who is to ever play full campaign from 39 to to 45?!? Nobody, never... Stealing much of ideas from The Second World War (2010).   THIRD REICH from 4 decades ago is in every aspect immeasurable better.

[Rating: 1/10] The combat result system, IMHO, needs to be reworked. The CRT is players competing against each other trying to roll the higher 6-sided die.  Extreme result can happen where a minor country unit can completely stop three German units, Armor Inf Inf with air support to fail.

[Rating: 2/10] Sold. I bought this last summer and just got around to digging into it. Sorry, I just can't get past the bizarre map. Who thought it was a good idea to distort the map aspect ratio by 30 - 50%? Whatever other qualities it may or may not have, this kills it for me.  For me an attractive functional map is important, and this one is neither. I have to wonder whether the distortion would impact tactics,  but I will not spend the time to find out. I was wondering if I had missed out on a "fix kit" when I opened it up, but I guess it's just bad.

[Rating: 2/10] Like the squat equal area projection map, some unusual abstractions that will endear it to the "what is different" crowd but in the end do not end up to a particular enticing game. It all seems to work somehow, but is too long for the abstractions it contains and seems to produce neither historical campaign speeds nor realistic strategic engagements.  Long, repetitive, a bit boring and pointless. [Rating: 2/10] The east front doesn't work out so well realistically when it's so simplified. I played too much Russian Campaign, 3rd Reich, and Barbarossa Campaign.

[Rating: 2/10] The map is a shame Oslo - Trondheim distance: 4 hexes Oslo - Bergen distance: 6 hexes (should be 3) When you play such a wargame (ETO), it must be on an historical basis and not with a map from another planet! Stupid idea

[Rating: 3/10] It has achieved lot in area of streamlining. It is easy to grasp and not bothered with details. I would even say that I am missing little bit of chrome.   Also game is too much process heavy and not very much fun for face to face play. I can imagine that people playing solitaire are enjoying it lot.   Although I do appreciate design I don't enjoy it and thus low rating.

[Rating: 3/10] Just too generic for my tastes. Some poorly named chits. No fog of war. No thanks.

[Rating: 3/10] Though different and in parts innovative, this is one process heavy game where mostly you bump armies across a map of Europe.  Full review: http://www.boardgamegeek.com/blogpost/43706

[Rating: 3/10] Played the first two scenarios and they are boring as sin.  This game seems to have some potential.

[Rating: 3/10] Unbearable setup time and one player has basically nothing to do for the first 1/3rd of the game.

[Rating: 4/10] A great deception. You have very few choices during all the campagne game. Diplomacy is a bit hazardous: Italy can join the Allies if Axis is lucky enough.

[Rating: 4/10] I really wanted to like/own this game, this is why I was so happy to see it on BGA. But my excitement haven't lasted long. The first 3 tutorial scenarios were OK, played and replayed them couple of times just to learn the rules. But the first real scenario, the Balkans '41 is really disappointed me. I realised how extremely luck based this game is. You have only 2 rounds to complete this scenario, so if you roll 2-3 "No effects", then that's it, no chance to win. Defeat. [Rating: 4/10] I was underwhelmed by the game. Played on BGA. Perhaps in person it would have been better. The various scenarios weren't really to my liking. The map and multiple chits are a little more than I'm looking for.was

[Rating: 4/10] For a grand strategy game, it lacks strategic options.  It seems to be driven in large part by luck with weather and political chit draws.  There is no agency over force composition, which is scripted.  Feel free to tell me where I got this wrong.
